patterns.note: The artist's name is presented as an oversized, fixed header that remains visible at the top of the viewport throughout the scroll.
Artworks are displayed in a flexible grid layout, often with a white border or frame effect, creating a gallery-like presentation.
The initial hero illustration shrinks and moves upwards, creating a parallax-like effect as the user scrolls, eventually revealing the content below.

The primary navigation bar initially appears below the hero illustration, then transitions to a sticky position at the top of the viewport, directly beneath the fixed artist name, after the hero has scrolled sufficiently.
A single, wide, monospaced sans-serif font is used consistently across all text elements, varying only in size and weight to establish hierarchy.
A vibrant and diverse color palette is used exclusively within the illustrative content, sharply contrasted against a minimal black and off-white user interface.

technique_notes: The main artist name at the top of the page is implemented as a fixed element, ensuring it always stays in view.
The hero illustration uses a scroll-triggered animation (likely css-keyframes) to scale down and translate upwards, creating a shrinking parallax effect as the user scrolls down the page.

The primary navigation bar is initially positioned relative to the content flow, then dynamically switches to a sticky position at the top of the viewport, just below the fixed header, once the initial hero section has scrolled out of its original position.

design_tokens.type_scale: Oversized, bold, wide monospaced hero heading (~5-6x body) with small, all-caps monospaced body and navigation text.
design_tokens.spacing: airy hero, balanced content grid with generous padding around individual artworks.

standout: This site's design is distinctive for its bold, fixed, oversized monospaced header combined with a dynamic, shrinking hero illustration that creates a unique parallax effect. The navigation's transition from below the hero to a sticky top position is also a clever touch, making the site feel like an interactive art gallery rather than a standard portfolio template.
